accepted_gaps.title: No decisive residual-specificity test of canonical meridian labels
accepted_gaps.why_open: Existing measurements show heterogeneous site effects and anatomical covariates, but do not test whether canonical labels add explanatory power after those covariates are controlled.

accepted_gaps.title: Clinical efficacy and meridian ontology are routinely confounded
accepted_gaps.why_open: A clinical effect does not by itself identify the pathway producing it; trials are not normally structured to distinguish a meridian-specific route from local anatomy, expectation, or generic somatosensory stimulation.

accepted_gaps.title: Competing anatomy, nerve, and fascial mechanisms lack a common falsification protocol
accepted_gaps.why_open: Measurements and models are typically evaluated in isolation, making it difficult to compare whether a named trajectory carries information beyond ordinary tissue variables.

candidate_gaps_not_accepted_as_facts.claim: Meridians are spaces rather than structures.
candidate_gaps_not_accepted_as_facts.reason: The 2020 article supports an interpretation, not unique structural validation.
